title: Prove complete clean six-tape multiplication and eight explicit applications
body:
One fixed finite six-tape machine now returns the exact padded product and erases all five other tapes for every valid input width, including zero. Exact six-phase setup accounting (40n + 30 physical transitions) gives the complete upper bound 280n² + 278n + 68, with actual terminal heads and genuine halt. This extends the retained toolkit/multiplication lineage in PRs #1641 and #2235.

The Mathlib-only public package adds explicit bounded dirty windows; independent tape-origin relocation; exact setup invoices; fixed injective alphabet transport; minimal Nat.size operand width with literal padding; ZMod/signed residue labels; designated-tape endpoint adapters; and accumulator-output multiplication with literally unchanged input ABI. Window, width/residue and accumulator theorem statements retain the conservative 280n² + 322n + 122 bound.

Validation: all 74 bundled proof modules plus the aggregator rebuilt in a fresh directory with Lean 4.34.1 against pinned Mathlib d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612. The complete defining-module/transitive-axiom audit covered 5,350 declarations, including 2,824 theorems and 547 private declarations; only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound are admitted. Four actual Lean ownership/axiom fixtures and source/operational controls passed. External dependency binaries are supplied source-revision-checked cache artifacts, not independently rebuilt. Hosted CI and independent human review are not claimed.

The input is two supplied LSB stack words, not a serialized/signed parser. Residue output is the full double-width natural product, not an executed truncation. The fixed tape permutation preserves operand ABI as an adapter; multiplication consumes the operands. This is quadratic execution infrastructure, not a new kappa or the full fast multiplication algorithm.

Refreshed main 8e22a9d9f621c72ab5b299061c2be4c7f638fd3c and 1,898 recently updated PR metadata records. Compared actual relevant sources, including existing alphabet/multiplication work linked by #2411 and paid return/output/widening/padding #2418/#2438/#2439/#2635/#2636. FRONTIER.md and reviews record substantial overlap and bounded coverage; no first-use claim. Existing arithmetic, compiler, PR64/1379/1641 and Mathlib attribution and licenses remain.

Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance included one root plus three parallel agents. Open next questions: charged serialized/signed parsing, marked-caller bank integration, and variable-depth physical recursion/routing.
